crop_profile.summary: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a globally important annual cereal grown on loamy to clay soils with pH 6.0-7.5. Optimal temperatures are 10-25 °C, rainfall 300-900 mm/year, and sunlight 6-10 h/day. It requires medium water and nitrogen, with critical moisture needs during flowering. Major producers include China, India, Russia, the United States, and France. Typical yields are 3 t/ha, reaching up to 7 t/ha under optimal management. Key diseases are Fusarium head blight, powdery mildew, and leaf rust; main pests include aphids, Hessian fly, and wheat midge. Integrated pest management, split nitrogen fertilization, and timely harvest ensure high quality grain.

recommendation.recommendation: Immediate field inspection to diagnose and address vegetation health decline
recommendation.justification: Satellite imagery shows critical NDVI (90) well below the poor threshold, indicating severe canopy loss. Combined with the risk of Fusarium head blight and powdery mildew, and potential nutrient deficiencies, an on‑ground assessment is essential to prevent yield loss, despite excellent soil conditions and favorable weather.
actions: Conduct a systematic walk‑through of the field, recording canopy cover, leaf discoloration, and any disease symptoms; note GPS locations of problem spots.
Collect leaf tissue samples from symptomatic and healthy plants for laboratory nutrient analysis.
If Fusarium head blight or powdery mildew symptoms are observed, apply the recommended fungicide (e.g., a triazole at flowering stage) following label rates.
Based on nutrient test results, apply a foliar nitrogen/phosphorus spray (e.g., 0.5% urea + 0.2% phosphoric acid) to deficient areas.
Increase soil surface protection by spreading crop residues or a light cover crop to reduce exposure and improve moisture retention.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Early detection and treatment will restore canopy vigor, limit disease spread, correct nutrient gaps, and protect soil moisture, thereby preserving yield potential and profitability for the upcoming harvest.
monitoring_plan: Re‑capture satellite NDVI (or drone NDVI) in 7 days to verify canopy recovery.
Perform visual disease scouting twice weekly for the next three weeks.
Re‑test leaf nutrient status 10 days after foliar application.
Monitor soil moisture daily and adjust irrigation if moisture drops below field capacity.
